history.sg_progress: The staff selection policy is being revised to simplify and streamline procedures as part of the Secretary-General’s management reform. In terms of transparency, the Administration confirms that all applications in the Inspira system are reviewed automatically for education, language and years of work experience and manually by human resources practitioners for suitable work experience and desirable criteria. With regard to shortening the recruitment process, as a result of enhancements to Inspira, managers are sent alerts to update them on the status of their recruitment processes, providing a breakdown of the number of applicants and the total number of days that the job opening has been posted against the target date for recruitment. At its seventy-first session, the General Assembly approved, on a pilot basis, a reduction from 60 to 45 days for the posting of position-specific job openings in the Professional and higher categories. At its seventy-third session, the General Assembly decided to defer until the seventy-fourth session consideration of a proposal to further reduce from 45 to 30 days the standard posting period for position-specific job openings in the Professional and higher categories. In September 2018, the United Nations Global Centre for Human Resources Services was established as part of the “OneHR” initiative to streamline and standardize human resources procedures in the United Nations system in the areas of reference verification and job classification.

history.sg_progress: As a result of the dual effect of the current staff selection policy and the delegation of authority framework under which both hiring responsibility and accountability are placed at entity level, the focus has been put on introducing incremental improvements in the recruitment process with the aim of making it more efficient, in accordance with, inter alia, General Assembly resolution 71/263 and as manifested in the shortening of the recruitment timeline. Those improvements have been carried out predominantly under the recruitment innovation project in place since 2019, which is both (a) bottleneck-driven in that it starts from a rigorous analysis of timelines at each stage and substage of the recruitment process and introduces improvements with the highest impact first and (b) client-centric in that priorities and needs are continuously discussed and identified together with entities. The Administration considers the recommendation to be implemented and requests its closure by the Board. D. history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration review the recruitment process to increase transparency and simplify and shorten the procedure.
history.administration_response: The Administration stated that to address the recommendation, the Office of Human Resources was developing a change programme: Staff Selection 2.0. The objective of the programme is to deliver processes, policies, tools and technologies for an effective staff selection system that ensures accuracy, fairness and efficiency. Staff Selection 2.0 will cover three components: recruitment, outreach and the Young Professionals Programme. The recruitment component is composed of three workstreams with multiple projects within and across them: (a) comprehensive job analysis and skill identification; (b) assessment methods and tools for now and the future; and (c) ensuring accountability and agility in staff selection. Subject to the availability of resources, the programme is due to be implemented by 2026. The end result of Staff Selection 2.0 is to enable the Organization to have a diverse and inclusive workforce that delivers on its evolving mandates. The new, streamlined staff selection system will also fulfil the letter and spirit of Article 101 of the Charter of the United Nations in recruiting staff on as a wide a geographical basis as possible.
history.board_assessment: Work is still ongoing. The Board considers the recommendation to be under implementation.

history.sg_progress: The Administration has taken a number of steps through the various revisions of the administrative instruction on the staff selection system (ST/AI/2010/3), as well as other administrative instructions, to ensure that the recruitment process is simpler and more transparent and that the overall procedure is shorter and adaptable to the current needs of the Organization. Notable updates include the amendment to the administrative instruction issued in 2017 (ST/AI/2010/3/Amend.3), by which the deadline of applying for regular job openings in the Professional and higher categories was reduced from 60 to 45 days. Furthermore, in 2023, the Administration issued an administrative instruction on downsizing or restructuring resulting in termination of appointments (ST/AI/2023/1), whereby it determined that no roster selections could be made for job openings or temporary job openings before the job opening posting period had closed. This will further reduce the overall recruitment timeline by enabling hiring managers to make selections faster. In 2018, the United Nations Global Centre for Human Resources Services was established in Bonn, Germany, to streamline and standardize and provide job classification advice and notices using the master standards promulgated by the International Civil Service Commission. In addition, the Centre launched a reference- checking process, through which employment background, academic records and qualitative references are checked. Lastly, automated tools were introduced in Inspira in 2019, specifically in relation to the screening process. These include the job fit questionnaire and an interview evaluation feature for expedited reporting on competency-based interviews. Another feature introduced in Inspira in 2019 was the candidate summary feature, which displays a summary of key data from the application profile and the job fit questionnaire on one page as well as analytics related to the diversity of the candidate pool. In 2020, the candidate summary was supplemented by the applied criteria tool to support the definition and recording of the methodology used by the hiring manager in the preliminary evaluation. Those recruitment innovations have enabled hiring managers to accelerate both the screening and evaluation processes. In view of the incremental revisions made to the staff selection system policy, process and technological tools since the recommendation was issued, the Administration requests closure of the recommendation. B. Recommendations contained in the report of the Board of Auditors for the 12-month period ended 30 June 2019 (A/74/5 (Vol. II), chap. II)
